text:
**Yes—under the tool’s corroboration rule**, the 2023 tree-cover loss is confirmed in the latest run. Hansen data identified 4.5 hectares of loss, a later year was observed, and the JRC reference mapped 100% of the event area as forest in 2020.

The 2021 national forest map classified 4.3 hectares of the event area as planted pine forest and 0.2 hectares as outside mapped forest; none was mapped as native forest. A further 1.3 hectares of loss occurred in patches below the 0.5-hectare event threshold and was not counted as an event.

The earlier 2024 run did not yet meet the corroboration rule because no later year had been observed. The evidence does not establish the cause of the loss.
